summary: Frontend-only test of the new persistent global OUT rail (HOME/RECAP/NEXT/STATS) on all detail routes. Onboarded (Boston Bruins). OUT rail is present with correct testIDs (out-home, out-recap, out-tonight, out-stats) on Team, League, Player, and Game pages, and Back button remains present. In-app tap of out-stats from a team page returns to the main shell with the STATS tab active (verified via color state), and out-home returns with the HOME tab active (home-show visible). Breadcrumbs (crumb-league -> /league/nhl and crumb-division -> /league/nhl?division=Atlantic) work. Player tap navigates to /player/{id}. Main top tabs still switch. All acceptance criteria for this NAV PASS ONE pass in the standard user flow.

issues: Last row of 'Leading the Way' (David Pastrnak) sits directly under the OUT rail on 390x844; last row can appear partially occluded until the user scrolls a bit. Consider adding bottom safe-area padding equal to OUT rail height (~52px) on Screen content so the last card clears the rail.

action_items: (Optional edge case, not in scope for this pass) Deep-linking directly to /team/BOS (hard page load) then tapping out-stats currently lands on the HOME tab of the shell (not STATS). Root cause: goToTab uses a module-level handler set by TabsHost useEffect; when the team page is the first mounted route, the handler is null, so setActive('stats') never runs before router.dismissAll() reveals the shell with default active='home'. If deep-link parity is desired later, persist the desired tab (AsyncStorage / URL param / a queue in tabnav.ts that is replayed once setTabHandler is called) so that when TabsHost mounts it can immediately select the requested tab.

(Optional polish) Bump ScrollView contentContainerStyle.paddingBottom on detail routes (team/player/game/league) by ~56px so the final row of scroll content isn't visually pinned under the persistent OUT rail.
critical_code_review_comments: src/components/ui.tsx OutRail: jump() correctly calls goToTab(key) BEFORE router.dismissAll(), so the tab is selected while TabsHost is still (or will be) mounted. For the normal in-app flow this is correct and observed to work.

src/lib/tabnav.ts is a fire-and-forget module singleton — if no TabsHost has mounted yet (deep link into a detail route), the goToTab call is a no-op. Consider queueing the last requested key and replaying it in setTabHandler(h) when a handler is finally provided.
seed_data_creation: None — completed real onboarding in the app (search 'Boston' -> Boston Bruins).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Onboarding search input requires page.keyboard.type (page.fill does not trigger the RN TextInput onChangeText). testIDs of interest: welcome-go, onboard-search, result-team-BOS, onboard-skip, onboard-next, toptab-home/recap/tonight/stats, out-home/out-recap/out-tonight/out-stats, back-button, crumb-league, crumb-division, team-next, next-team-{ABBR}, league-team-{ABBR}, leader-{playerId}, open-game, game-play-the-call. NEXT tab's testID is 'out-tonight' (label 'NEXT'). To reach the team page in-app, click toptab-stats and scroll the standings ScrollView until 'Bruins' text is on-screen. Player rows in 'Leading the Way' have no testID; click via JS-walk-up to the pressable (role=button / cursor:pointer). Multiple OUT rails may appear in DOM at once when Stack keeps previous detail routes mounted on web — visually only one is shown; treat as expected React Navigation Stack behavior on web, not a bug.
